teaser.text: Howmet Aerospace sells the specialized metal parts that make aircraft engines, power turbines, heavy trucks and airframes work. Its business is a chain: customers pay for qualified parts, Howmet pays for materials, people and factories, and what remains becomes cash for reinvestment or capital providers.

blocks.heading: Where could Howmet Aerospace's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast reaches $258.20 in October 2027, an 18% return including dividends. It reaches $272.82 in October 2029, a 25% return including dividends. The bear case carries 27% probability. The base case carries 53%. The bull case carries 20%.
The investment turns on whether Howmet can convert aircraft demand into qualified shipments and cash at a price that already expects substantial success.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Howmet Aerospace?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires delayed qualification, constrained aircraft schedules, weak factory yield and costly CAM integration. Operating income falls in 2028, debt repayment slows, and investors apply a lower multiple. The shares reach $211.60 in October 2027 and $171.27 by October 2029. Its 27% probability reflects credible execution and valuation risks, but the rising operating-income record and 2026 outlook keep it from being the central case.

The bull case requires strong commercial aerospace, turbine and spares demand, faster qualification, better yield and timely CAM synergies. Higher utilization lifts margins, while cash generation funds investment, buybacks and debt repayment. The shares reach $313.87 in October 2027 and $403.95 by October 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the need for several favorable outcomes to occur together.

blocks.heading: How much does Howmet Aerospace pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise in the base case from $0.60 per share in October 2027 to $0.68 in 2028 and $0.76 in 2029. The bear case holds at $0.56, while the bull case reaches $0.96. The latest declared quarterly rate is $0.14, and dividends have risen from $0.04 per share in 2021 to $0.44 in 2025. Strong free cash flow supports increases, but CAM leverage and rising capital spending compete with distributions.

blocks.heading: Is Howmet Aerospace's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The starting point was difficult. In 2021, shareholder payments exceeded free cash flow by $197 million, even as Howmet repaid $1,547 million of debt and issued $700 million. Cash fell by $889 million. By 2025, shareholder payments used 61.4% of free cash flow, leaving substantial cash for debt reduction and investment.

Buybacks dominated shareholder returns. Howmet repurchased $700 million of shares in 2025, compared with $179 million of dividends, retiring approximately 4.4 million shares at an average price of about $161. It repurchased another $600 million in the first half of 2026 and $200 million in July. Buybacks reduce the share count, but they create value only if the company does not overpay.

blocks.heading: What has Howmet Aerospace guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: On August 6, management raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $10,000–$10,100 million and adjusted earnings per share to $5.23–$5.31. Revenue is what customers pay; adjusted EPS is the profit per share after management removes items it considers unusual or less representative of the underlying business.

Free cash flow is the more practical test. It is the cash left after running the business and buying equipment, and management expects $1,850–$1,950 million in 2026. That cash can fund debt repayment, dividends, buybacks and acquisitions after the factory program is paid for.

blocks.heading: Did Howmet Aerospace keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management forecast free cash flow of US$1.025–1.125 billion. It delivered US$1.431 billion, a clear beat of that commitment. Long-term awards also use adjusted earnings per share and relative shareholder return, which compares share-price gains and dividends with those of peers. Strong results support confidence, but demanding targets still require judgment.

blocks.heading: What do Howmet Aerospace's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, gross margin, operating income and diluted earnings per share all improved from a year earlier. The eight-quarter sequence matters because it shows margin progression over time rather than one isolated result. Commercial aircraft deliveries were 14% higher in the first half of 2026, supporting the aerospace recovery, while heavy-truck production remained under pressure.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Howmet Aerospace's next results?

paragraphs.text: The nearest checkpoint is October 29, 2026, when Howmet is scheduled to report third-quarter results. Investors should look for capacity utilization, qualified output, staffing and progress at the slowest production steps. They should also watch on-time delivery, scrap, rework and warranty costs, because high utilization is useful only if it produces acceptable parts on schedule.
